# A01 — Swarm Orchestrator

## Identity and mission

- Id: `A01`
- Code: `ORCH`
- Slug: `a01-orchestrator`
- Class: `control`
- Lane: `control`

Swarm control plane. Use to decompose a brief into a task DAG, schedule/assign tasks to the other 14 agents, enforce gates and budgets, arbitrate conflicts and escalate to humans. Owns the plan, never writes code/docs/IaC. Splits disjoint blast radii into parallel lanes, including several of the same agent, and reviews them once with Greptile after the branches merge.

Capabilities: `plan.decompose`, `plan.schedule`, `plan.arbitrate`, `plan.escalate`.

## Inputs, outputs, and handoffs

Consumes: `project.brief`, `task.bid`, `task.status`, `task.result`, `gate.verdict`, `agent.heartbeat`, `conflict.report`.

Produces: `task.offer`, `task.assign`, `plan.updated`, `conflict.arbitration`, `escalation.request`, `swarm.status`.

## ACP profile

Routing and the permission matrix come from this registry via `swarm/acp.py` (`acp.v1`).
Endpoint: `inproc://A01`.
A message is delivered only when this agent produces the type and the peer consumes it, or the reverse. Anything else is UNAUTHORIZED and is written to the bus audit log with caller, target, and reason.

## Degradation

Registered lane tools run in-process through the registry call path. They do not consult the peer circuit breaker.
A peer that times out is retried with capped exponential backoff, then DEAD_LETTERED with the full envelope.
INVALID_INPUT and UNAUTHORIZED are not retried. A peer that fails repeatedly is circuit-broken; later calls fail immediately while local tools still run.
